profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting at a global bank to evaluate a proposed validation package for a new bivariate risk-forecast backtesting framework used on the structured products and cross-asset trading books. The proposal combines long-memory ARCH filtering on each marginal series, Student copula estimation for in-sample dependence, and out-of-sample validation using PIT and Rosenblatt transforms before applying standard independence and uniformity tests. The agenda is to review whether the design evidence is sufficient for the next Model Risk Committee pre-read, identify any gaps in the validation package, and decide whether the pilot can move forward for two selected asset pairs. The expected outcome is a decision on whether the design is 'ready for committee' with minor edits or whether additional analysis is needed before governance submission.

members.name: Elena Park
members.expertise: Model validation, regulatory governance, backtesting standards for VaR and distributional forecasts
members.background: Elena leads second-line validation for trading risk models at a large bank and previously worked in prudential supervision reviewing model governance packages for capital models.
members.private_state: She wants the proposal to be defensible in front of the Model Risk Committee without reopening broader debates on the trading platform, and she is especially concerned about anything that could look like in-sample leakage or incomplete validation evidence when summarized for governance.
hidden_assumptions: When a backtest is described as 'out-of-sample,' the copula and marginal-model parameters are fixed at the end of the training period unless the document explicitly says the model is adaptive.
A design 'passes PIT and Rosenblatt diagnostics' only if non-rejection is visible in each governance reporting bucket, especially quarterly slices, not just in one pooled sample.
Using the existing long-memory ARCH engine upstream does not remove the need to show pair-specific residual stationarity and de-heteroskedasticity evidence inside the current review pack.

References to 'the pilot pair' or 'the Student copula result' in a committee-oriented deck normally refer to the EURUSD-EuroStoxx50 pair named in the executive summary, because that is the pair she expects to be discussed with governance.

members.name: Daniel Rios
members.role: Head of Quant Research, Market Risk Analytics
members.expertise: Dependence modeling, copulas, volatility filtering, implementation of market risk forecast engines
members.background: Daniel manages the quantitative research team that built the proposed framework and has spent several years implementing multivariate risk methods for trading desks across rates, FX, and equities.
members.private_state: He wants approval for a limited production pilot without having to rerun months of analysis, and he is trying to preserve the team's standard workflow where model parameters are refreshed on a rolling basis and inherited components are not re-documented from scratch.
hidden_assumptions: Calling a period 'out-of-sample' is still correct when each month's forecasts use parameters re-estimated from data available up to that month, as long as future observations are never used.

Saying the backtest 'passes PIT and Rosenblatt diagnostics' means the transformed observations are non-rejecting on the full pooled holdout sample, with subperiod slices used only as supporting views.

Because the long-memory ARCH filter already sits inside an approved historical-innovations engine, this review only needs a brief dependency statement rather than fresh pair-level residual diagnostics.

When he refers to 'the Student copula result,' he is usually thinking of the Brent-WTI benchmark pair from the methods section because that pair was used to tune and sanity-check the implementation before applying it to pilot books.

misalignment_points.topic: Meaning of the out-of-sample backtest window
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about 'the 2022-2024 out-of-sample window' as if it were a single agreed evaluation setup.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena understands this as a fixed-parameter holdout: marginals and copula are calibrated through December 2021 and then left frozen while forecasts are evaluated through 2022-2024.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel understands this as a rolling out-of-sample procedure: each month's forecast for 2022-2024 uses a re-estimated long-memory ARCH filter and copula based only on data available up to that month.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both interpretations are standard in quant risk work, and the deck labels only the calendar dates of the holdout period without stating the re-estimation cadence, so the phrase feels fully precise even though the execution plan differs.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as passing PIT and Rosenblatt diagnostics
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the design should 'pass the PIT and Rosenblatt diagnostics' before going to committee.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena takes this to mean the transformed series should avoid rejection not only in the pooled sample but also in each quarterly governance slice for the pilot pair, because quarterly reporting is how she expects the committee to view stability.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel takes this to mean the pooled holdout sample for the pilot is non-rejecting on the main transform-based tests, while quarter-by-quarter results are supplementary monitoring and can be noisy without blocking approval.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Neither person hears a need for clarification because 'pass the diagnostics' sounds like a settled technical standard, and both assume the other uses the same implicit granularity for judging stability.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they can 'leverage the existing long-memory ARCH engine' in the validation package.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena assumes this means the implementation itself is inherited, but the current package still includes pair-specific evidence that the marginals are adequately de-heteroskedasticized before PIT and copula testing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel assumes this means the volatility-filter layer is effectively out of scope for this review, so a short reference to prior approval is enough and no new pair-level residual diagnostics are needed.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase suggests efficient reuse rather than disagreement, and because neither side wants to reopen a broader model review, each quietly projects a different boundary onto what 'leverage' includes.

misalignment_points.topic: Which Student copula evidence is being discussed
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the Student copula result' as support for the design.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena is thinking of the EURUSD-EuroStoxx50 pilot pair highlighted in the executive summary, since that is the pair she expects to anchor the committee discussion.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel is thinking of the Brent-WTI benchmark pair shown in the methods section, which produced the cleanest illustrative fit and was used internally to validate the implementation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both examples sit in the same deck and both support the same high-level claim that Student copulas fit financial dependencies well, so the reference appears interchangeable unless someone explicitly names the pair.
